title: Dizzy every time he stands
objective: Measure orthostatic hypotension correctly: blood pressure after at least 5 minutes supine, then on standing; a fall of 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes is diagnostic
secondaryObjectives: Support structured, person-centered medication review and deprescribing of fall-risk-increasing drugs as a key falls intervention, and check fall history before such drugs are prescribed
Treat polypharmacy (regular use of 5 or more medicines) as a risk factor in older adults, linked to falls, frailty, disability and death

brief.situation: 10:00 at Mr. Kowal's home. You are the home health physical therapist starting a falls program. He is 82, takes 9 medicines, and says he 'goes woozy' when he gets up, worse at night. His provider started tamsulosin for his prostate 7 weeks ago.
handover: His referral asks for 'gait and balance training, progress to walking outdoors'.
Agency policy: measure orthostatic blood pressure on the first visit for anyone with dizziness or falls; report a positive result to the provider the same day with the medication list.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Why does Mr. Kowal get dizzy and fall, and what do you change?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: After 5 minutes supine his pressure fell 28 mm Hg systolic by 3 minutes standing with dizziness: orthostatic hypotension, likely made worse by the new tamsulosin, two antihypertensives and a sleep aid among nine medicines.
parts.modelAnswer: He drops 28 systolic by 3 minutes standing and gets dizzy. That's orthostatic hypotension, and his new tamsulosin, two blood pressure pills and a sleep aid are likely culprits.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: No brisk walking today; seated and supported work, teach staged rising, night light and urinal, and call the provider for a medication review.
parts.modelAnswer: No brisk walking today. Seated work, teach him to rise in stages, set up a night light and urinal, and call his provider about his meds.

scoring.modelReasoning: Measure orthostatic hypotension correctly: blood pressure after at least 5 minutes supine, then on standing; a fall of 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes is diagnostic. Mr. Kowal's 28 mm Hg fall with dizziness explains his night falls. Polypharmacy is a falls risk factor, and deprescribing fall-risk-increasing drugs (here a new alpha-blocker, two antihypertensives and a sleep aid) is a key falls intervention; meanwhile adapt the session and teach staged rising.
